First, we recall the following identities: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }
$$

Using the above identity, we can simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{csc}^{2}⁡\theta {tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{sec}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\frac{{sin}^{4}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{4}⁡\theta }-\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{4}⁡\theta }-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}\frac{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{4}⁡\theta }-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta {tan}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta ({sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ({sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1) & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={tan}^{4}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{csc}^{2}⁡\theta {tan}^{4}⁡\theta -{sec}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡\theta ={tan}^{4}⁡\theta .
$$
